definition: A distributed training technique that splits a model's layers across multiple devices, with different devices processing different stages of the forward and backward pass in a pipelined fashion.
details: Pipeline parallelism complements data and model (tensor) parallelism, together forming the combination of parallelization strategies used to train today's largest language models across thousands of accelerators.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. Boil it down and it is this: A distributed training technique that splits a model's layers across multiple devices, with different devices processing different stages of the forward and backward pass in a pipelined fashion. Here is why it matters: Pipeline parallelism complements data and model (tensor) parallelism, together forming the combination of parallelization strategies used to train today's largest language models across thousands of accelerators. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Pipeline Parallelism.
